hypotheses.rationale: Day 12 (Saturday) shows a return to the rigid Mon-Thu wake-up time (06:46) and kitchen-centric routine (no desk usage). This contradicts the 'WFH Friday' sub-hypothesis as the weekend does not mimic the Friday WFH pattern. The consistent early rise and lack of commute indicators across all observed days strongly favor a general remote worker or someone with a very flexible but early-rising schedule.

Still possible if the resident works from home on Fridays but commutes Mon-Thu and weekends. However, the lack of any 'commute prep' items (keys, bag) on Mon-Thu makes this less likely than pure remote work. The Saturday routine is indistinguishable from Mon-Thu, offering no new evidence to support this over the primary hypothesis.

Discarded. The consistent early wake-ups (06:45-07:08) and structured daily meal/cleanup times contradict irregular or night-shift schedules. No study materials or late-night activity indicators observed.
